slides.title: FraudSociety: A Generative Agent-Based Society for the Financial-Fraud Economy
slides.highlight: FraudSociety introduces an LLM-agent-based simulator that jointly models informational and financial dynamics in fraud economies, offering a scalable testbed for evaluating anti-fraud interventions.

card.one_liner: FraudSociety is an LLM-agent simulator jointly modeling informational and financial dynamics of fraud.
card.key_idea: Integrates dynamic social graphs, persistent financial ledgers, and a Need-Intent-Action architecture to couple information exposure with financial outcomes.
card.evaluation: Validated via Quartet Distance against FTC stats, micro-level loss concentration, and five counter-fraud interventions using 112 civilians and 8 fraudsters.
card.limitation: Relies on Qwen3-14B for agent decisions, potentially limiting behavioral fidelity compared to larger models or human data.

slides.title: Simulation-Efficient Double-Flow Neural Posterior Estimation for Agent-Based Models
slides.highlight: This work introduces Double-Flow Neural Posterior Estimation (DF-NPE), which reduces the computational cost of Bayesian inference in agent-based models by up to 90% using synthetic data augmentation, directly addressing the scalability challenges of simulating complex hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: DF-NPE reduces agent-based model simulation costs by 90% using synthetic data augmentation for neural posterior estimation.
card.key_idea: Combines learned time-series summaries with two conditional normalizing flows to generate synthetic training pairs, supplementing direct simulations.
card.evaluation: Tested on Brock-Hommes asset-pricing model; compared against standard NPE using Wasserstein distance and MMD metrics against ground-truth posteriors.
card.limitation: Performance varies significantly with the allocation ratio of direct to synthetic data and the chosen training strategy.

slides.title: Multimodal Socially Aware Framework for Human-Robot Interaction in Virtual Reality
slides.highlight: This paper evaluates a multimodal framework integrating speech, vision, and touch for social robots, offering insights into the challenges of achieving natural interaction comparable to human teleoperation.

card.one_liner: A multimodal VR framework integrating speech, vision, and touch for socially aware robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Uses a VLM to process speech, vision, and touch inputs, generating coordinated robot actions and speech with interaction history.
card.evaluation: 18 participants in VR compared autonomous system to teleoperated baseline; autonomous rated lower in naturalness and appropriateness.
card.limitation: VR simulation may not fully capture physical robot dynamics; teleoperator familiarity and TTS prosody bias results.

slides.title: Agent-Based Transport Model Calibration via Online Stochastic Batch Optimization
slides.highlight: This paper introduces an online calibration framework for agent-based models that reduces computational burden by estimating parameters within a single simulation run, relevant to MIMIC's need for efficient meso-scale simulation methods.

card.one_liner: Calibrates agent-based transport models within a single simulation run using online stochastic batch optimization.
card.key_idea: Embeds parameter updates into MATSim iterations by treating replanning agents as stochastic batches, enabling co-evolution of parameters and behavior.
card.evaluation: Validated on a large-scale Swiss transport scenario; mode shares aligned with observed data within a standard simulation timeframe.
card.limitation: Relies on a quasi-static assumption that network conditions remain stable between iterations, which may fail in highly dynamic systems.

slides.title: Context-Aware Generation and Modulation of Expressive Motion Behavior using Multimodal Foundation Models
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how multimodal foundation models can generate context-aware, expressive full-body gestures for robots, directly supporting RwB's focus on embodied social interaction and AI-mediated learning.

card.one_liner: Context-aware expressive robot motion generation via multimodal foundation models and knowledge distillation.
card.key_idea: Generates and modulates Dynamic Movement Primitives using multimodal context, applying knowledge distillation for low-latency inference.
card.evaluation: User study with Pepper robot compared against non-modulated and API baselines; demonstrated cross-morphology versatility and reduced latency.
card.limitation: Relies on pre-recorded gesture libraries and specific robot kinematic parameters for motion primitive encoding.

slides.title: CEMIR vs. FISER: a comparative study of reasoning-based and enrichment-based approaches to pragmatic intent recognition
slides.highlight: This study compares structured social reasoning against multimodal enrichment for resolving ambiguous instructions in human-robot interaction, finding no significant performance difference when ambiguity concerns unstated intent rather than missing scene data. It highlights that backbone capability and ambiguity difficulty are more critical than synthetic multimodal augmentation in such contexts.

card.one_liner: Synthetic multimodal enrichment offers no significant advantage over structured reasoning for resolving pragmatic intent ambiguity.
card.key_idea: CEMIR enriches textual episodes with generated narratives and images, contrasting with FISER's structured social and embodied reasoning on the same text.
card.evaluation: Compared FISER and CEMIR on HandMeThat v2 across four LLMs and difficulty levels using paired permutation tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction.
card.limitation: Findings may not generalize to tasks requiring genuine external perceptual grounding, as enrichment was derived solely from existing text.

slides.title: Navigating human-robot interaction challenges in private and residential aged care homes
slides.highlight: This work addresses human-robot interaction in aged care settings, focusing on embodied systems for social engagement and design strategies for accessibility and trust, which aligns with RwB's goals for embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Review of HRI challenges in aged care, proposing privacy-by-design and real-world evaluation metrics.
card.key_idea: Frames care homes as extreme HRI environments; advocates hybrid robot-sensor systems with robust, simple interfaces and privacy-by-design safeguards.
card.evaluation: Proposes metrics like false alarms per day, staff workload, and fault recovery time, moving beyond accuracy to real-world reliability and usability.
card.limitation: Primarily a technical review; lacks empirical validation of proposed strategies and acknowledges unresolved challenges in robust perception and long-term engagement.

slides.title: RoleHear: Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Role-Attributed Streaming Speech Recognition
slides.tldr: Streaming ASR with inline role attribution
slides.highlight: This work addresses the challenge of attributing speaker roles in real-time streaming speech recognition, a key component for modeling group dynamics and addressee relationships in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: RoleHear enables semi-supervised streaming speech recognition with inline role attribution via pseudo-labeling.
card.key_idea: A streaming transducer emits role tokens inline using decoupled turn markers and delayed role values, trained via single-pass pseudo-labeling from an offline teacher.
card.evaluation: Tested on Earnings-21/22 (silver labels) and ServiceCall (gold labels); metrics include WER, RWER, and F1, showing improved role accuracy over baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on MLLM-generated silver labels for public data, introducing potential noise, and requires a separate offline teacher model for pseudo-label generation.

slides.title: Behavioural Quality Is Not Learning Utility: Objective Mismatch in Human Behaviour Models for Robot Learning
slides.highlight: This paper highlights an objective mismatch in human behavior models for robot learning, showing that behavioral fidelity does not consistently predict downstream policy performance in HRI domains like object handover. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning, as it questions the utility of current simulation methods for training interactive agents.

card.one_liner: Human behavior model realism metrics fail to predict downstream RL policy performance in HRI tasks.
card.key_idea: Evaluates rule-based and data-driven human models via generative metrics against RL policy performance in driving and handover tasks.
card.evaluation: Tested on highD and handover@RPL datasets; compared FD, KL, and diversity metrics with Deep Q-Learning policy returns.
card.limitation: Results are domain-specific; training against non-realistic distributions may yield better policies than realistic ones.

slides.title: FLAIR launches Hong Kong’s first embodied AI research hub
slides.highlight: The establishment of a dedicated embodied AI research hub in Hong Kong signals growing regional investment in the field, offering potential opportunities for collaboration and knowledge exchange relevant to embodied robotics initiatives.

slides.title: YYForce Inc. Announces Plan to Deploy First Humanoid Robot at Novotel Singapore on Stevens Amid Tesla Optimus Production Milestone
slides.highlight: The deployment of a humanoid robot in a hospitality setting highlights emerging trends in human-robot interaction and service automation, relevant to the development of embodied social robots.

slides.title: Tairex Launches Multi-Agent AI System to Transform Clinical Collaboration and Decision Support
slides.highlight: Tairex has launched a multi-agent AI system designed to enhance clinical collaboration and decision support, offering insights into agent-based architectures that parallel MIMIC's focus on modeling interactions within hybrid human-AI societies.

slides.title: Lipi-Ghor: A Large-Scale, Diarized, Multi-Domain Bengali Speech Corpus and a Scalable Pipeline for Building It
slides.highlight: This work introduces a large-scale, speaker-diarized Bengali speech corpus with long-form audio annotations, addressing gaps in low-resource language data relevant to HyECHO's focus on social perception and diarization.

card.one_liner: Lipi-Ghor is an 885-hour diarized Bengali speech corpus built from YouTube with a scalable pipeline.
card.key_idea: Constructs a large-scale Bengali ASR corpus by curating YouTube channels, extracting captions, and applying automated speaker diarization.
card.evaluation: Benchmarked four ASR models zero-shot and fine-tuned; validated via a 30-hour human-annotated gold split across 17 domains.
card.limitation: Weak supervision from noisy YouTube captions; diarization uses a commercial API; regional dialect coverage is sparse.

slides.title: NextEval: An Agent-Based Solver and Benchmark for Derivative-Free Optimization
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how LLM-based agents can effectively guide sequential decision-making in complex optimization tasks, a capability relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for simulating hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: An LLM agent guides derivative-free optimization by selecting numerical tools and allocating evaluation budgets.
card.key_idea: Integrates an LLM agent with a numerical environment; the agent analyzes history to select tools, configure parameters, and manage state for sequential point evaluation.
card.evaluation: Tested on 92 low-dimensional S2MPJ problems with perturbed/rotated/noisy settings; outperforms COBYQA and NEWUOA in evaluation efficiency.
card.limitation: Restricted to low-dimensional problems (n≤5); gains may stem from system design rather than LLM reasoning alone; high computational cost.
